title: UHR-BAT: Budget-Aware Token Compression Vision-Language model for Ultra-High-Resolution Remote Sensing
claim: Our method reaches top-tier accuracy while using far fewer inputs than comparably accurate models, sitting on the efficiency frontier.
layout: Single bubble scatter plot, accuracy vs token count, ours starred top-left
description: A single bubble scatter plot. The x-axis is the number of visual tokens (0 to 16000, plus a shaded 'Unknown' column on the right). The y-axis is performance, from about 20 to 45. Each model is a circle. Circle size shows parameter count (7B, 8B, 72B, 78B, unknown), with a size legend at top left. Color shows model type: filled blue for remote sensing models, orange outline for open-source models, grey outline for closed-source models. The proposed method, UHR-BAT, is a red-outlined star with a blue center in the top-left, with the highest accuracy at a low token count of about 3,400. Larger models such as InternVL3-78B and LLaVA-OneVision-72B sit further right at similar or lower accuracy. Closed-source models are in the shaded Unknown column. Dotted gridlines run behind the points, and a model-type legend sits at bottom right.
caption: Accuracy--efficiency frontier for Ultra-High-Resolution Remote Sensing MLLMs on XLRS-Bench benchmark. We report overall weighted average accuracy versus the number of visual tokens. The results show that our method achieves superior performance using fewer tokens.
abstract: Ultra-high-resolution (UHR) remote sensing imagery couples kilometer-scale context with query-critical evidence that may occupy only a few pixels. Such vast spatial scale leads to a quadratic explosion of visual tokens and hinders the extraction of information from small objects. Previous works utilize direct downsampling, dense tiling, or global top-k pruning, which either compromise query-critical image details or incur unpredictable compute. In this paper, we propose UHR-BAT, a query-guided and region-faithful token compression framework to efficiently select visual tokens under a strict context budget. Specifically, we leverage text-guided, multi-scale importance estimation for visual tokens, effectively tackling the challenge of achieving precise yet low-cost feature extraction. Furthermore, by introducing region-wise preserve and merge strategies, we mitigate visual token redundancy, further driving down the computational budget. Experimental results show that UHR-BAT achieves state-of-the-art performance across various benchmarks. Code will be available at https://github.com/Yunkaidang/UHR.
